description:
So many people think fame is what damages people - but the deeper truth is this: people who already feel wounded, inadequate, or not enough can be incredibly drawn to fame because they believe it will finally make them feel whole.

Fame does not heal the cracks - it magnifies them.

When someone does not feel enough inside, they can become vulnerable to poor judgment, unhealthy dynamics, and believing things they desperately want to be true.

No amount of attention, status, or visibility can give you the self-worth you have not yet built within yourself.

Real security does not come from being seen by everyone else - it comes from feeling safe, worthy, and enough within yourself. 💛

Damaged people are very drawn to fame. We've seen Katie Price saying that her husband was kidnapped but managed to, with a hood on and his hands bound, take a photograph of himself, which is kind of impossible. If you've got a hood on and your hands are bound, how can you get your phone out of your pocket and take a photo? And by the way, the people kidnapping you would search you and take away your phone immediately because you could probably track it. So it doesn't make sense. People who are desperate for fame do desperate things. They don't listen to their own judgment. They believe things that are really too good to be true. We have people who feel inadequate, who believe they're broken, who think that being famous will fix all the cracks and make them better. And it doesn't, it just makes those cracks bigger. I feel very sorry for Katie. She doesn't deserve this, but she's been taken in.
